The stranger came early in February, one wintry day, through a biting wind and a driving
snow, the last snowfall of the year. Over the down, walking from Bramblehurst Railway Station
and carrying a little black portmanteau in his thickly gloved hand. He was wrapped up from
head to foot, and the brim of his soft felt hat hid every inch of his face but the shiny
tip of his nose. The snow had piled itself against his shoulders and chest and added
a white crest to the burden he carried. He staggered into the coach and horses more dead
than alive and flung his portmanteau down. A fire, he cried, in the name of human charity,

and a couple of sovereigns flung upon the table, he took up his quarters in the inn. Mrs.
